$comment: HAND-TRANSCRIBED from each endpoint's PUBLIC model page (https://fal.ai/models/<id>). fal publishes no
machine-readable price anywhere — not in the Platform API, not in the OpenAPI document — so every rate here
is a human reading a sentence and writing down what it said, which is why each row carries the exact `quote`
it was read from, the `source` URL it was read at, and the date it was `verified`.
A curated endpoint with neither a rate nor an `unpriced` reason FAILS codegen. Silence about price is the one
thing this file may not say.
Row shape — either a rate:
unit      per_image | per_megapixel | per_second | per_video_minute | per_30_seconds |
per_1000_characters | per_audio_minute | tiered | conditional | compute_second
usd       the scalar rate in that unit (absent for tiered/conditional — see `tiers`)
rounding  how fal rounds the billed quantity, verbatim from the page (e.g. megapixels round UP)
tierKey   what selects the tier (a wire field name, or prose when it is not one field)
tiers     [{ when, usd }] — the rates, each labelled by the condition that selects it
source / verified / quote
…or an explicit non-price:
unpriced  the REASON no rate can be stated, in prose
source / verified / quote
WHICH UNITS REACH `ModelCost` — deliberately only four, the ones `src/core/catalog-types.ts` can express
exactly, per src/providers/HAND_CATALOGS.md:
per_image           → cost.perImage
per_second          → cost.perVideoSecond
per_1000_characters → cost.perMillionCharacters (×1000 — exact, not a conversion factor)
per_audio_minute    → cost.perAudioMinute
Every other unit — per_megapixel, per_video_minute, per_30_seconds, tiered, conditional, compute_second —
emits NO `cost` on the generated row, and the rate survives as a provenance comment above it instead.
`ModelCost` is not widened in wave 1: a per-megapixel rate written into `perImage` would be a number that
is wrong for every image that is not exactly one megapixel, and `undefined` beats a wrong number.
Tiered and conditional rates land in the hand pricing table (kling precedent), never here.
Verified 2026-08-24 against the live pages.
Of the 54 rows here, 12 carry a unit `ModelCost` can express and therefore reach a generated catalog
row; the other 42 do not, which is the shape of fal's pricing rather than a gap in this file. The
big classes: per_megapixel (11) needs the output's pixel count, which a request states only when it
writes `image_size: { width, height }` and not when it names a preset; conditional (15) needs a
field the request often leaves at its default; tiered (3) needs a quantity the request does not
state. All of them reach an ESTIMATE through gen/pricing.gen.ts and src/providers/fal/pricing.ts,
which computes what it can and returns `undefined` — with a reason available from `falPriceNote` —
for the rest. A plausible number that is wrong is worse than no number: a caller who sees `costUSD`
treats it as a budget.
